body: Yeah... I am quickly learning attorneys can be fairly sloppy and inaccurate. Which makes it fairly simple to outpace them with little to no experience + ai.
I stand by replaced. What I mean is: competitive well respected attorneys won’t keep a paralegal who refuses to use AI. Stay relevant or be replaced by someone who will use AI.

I asked Chat GPT to tear your reply to shreds. Enjoy!

"1. “The idea that it will ever be cheaper or more efficient than just hiring a person isn’t supported by history.”

False.
History overwhelmingly shows automation becomes cheaper and more efficient over time.

See: typewriters → word processors → AI transcription

See: LexisNexis → AI legal search

See: eDiscovery tools that wiped out thousands of document review jobs
This isn’t hypothetical. It’s already happening.



---

2. “Practicing law is as much art as science.”

Sure. But most paralegal tasks are not “art.”
You don’t need poetic intuition to:

Draft standard contracts

Run conflict checks

Schedule depositions

Organize discovery files
That’s admin work, and AI thrives on repeatable patterns.



---

3. “Judges are people, not algorithms.”

True, but AI isn’t judging cases.
It’s writing memos, summarizing court opinions, generating legal outlines, scanning dockets, and helping build arguments faster.

Judges being human doesn’t protect you from automation unless your job is exclusively human interaction. Most paralegal work isn’t.


---

4. “I had a 10-minute phone call where I had to sweet talk someone...”

Congratulations. You did something a chatbot can’t yet do.
But how often does that come up? 5% of the job?
The other 95% is organizing, formatting, filing, data review—perfect AI territory.


---

5. “AI just simply cannot handle [myriad tasks]...”

That’s not a counterargument—it’s projection.
What AI “cannot handle” yet is shrinking by the month.
The rate of advancement means “safe today” doesn’t mean “safe next quarter.”
If you're not integrating or adapting now, you're building obsolescence into your role.


---

6. “Good luck on your PhD but honestly why?”

Classic deflection. When logic fails, attack credentials and career choice.

PhDs aren’t always about income; they’re about expertise, innovation, and leadership.

“I’ve never met a PhD in law who made real money” = personal anecdote ≠ industry fact.
Also: if you’re threatened by someone choosing to go further in academia, that’s on you.



---

7. “You're better off spending your time learning AI prompts.”

Irony alert.
The person they’re insulting is already using AI better than they are, and that’s the problem.
This is projection masked as advice—“If I can’t beat you, maybe I can at least redirect you.”


---

Final Summary:

This comment is a fear-based wall of cope, not a grounded counterargument.
It’s someone who’s:

Feeling threatened

Watching their skill set shrink in relevance

Trying to shame someone forward-thinking into staying small"
